clue.text: Some maniac curate lying? Precisely!

indicators.note: Some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A suspicious question about whether a deranged clergyman is telling lies, answered with an emphatic agreement.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Some' signals that the answer sits inside the words that follow: maniAC CURATE LYing.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean exactly or without error, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Performance originally advertised in official documents

parts.note: an act is a performance on stage

indicators.note: originally points to the opening letter of the word advertised

explanation.surface: A show first promoted in formal papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Acta are official records or proceedings, the Latin plural of actum.

clue.text: Scotsman gets nothing out of African country

indicators.note: out of here says the zero letter is removed from the country's name

parts.note: Cameroon is a country in west-central Africa
O looks like zero, nothing

explanation.surface: A Scot comes home empty-handed from an African country.
explanation.definitionFit: Cameron is a Scottish clan name, so a Cameron is an example of a Scotsman.

clue.text: Horrid dog Enid trained as a little girl

indicators.note: trained suggests the letters are drilled into a new order, as a dog is taught tricks

explanation.surface: A nasty dog called Enid was trained to behave like a small girl.
explanation.definitionFit: The fairy-tale heroine with the red cape is a little girl who meets a wolf, apt beside the dog.

clue.text: Records attempt that has been made to present pictorial story?

definitions.text: that has been made to present pictorial story

parts.note: tapes are recordings
a try is an attempt

explanation.surface: Recordings are an effort made to tell a story in pictures.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is descriptive: a woven hanging such as the Bayeux one tells a story in pictures.
explanation.definitionFit: A woven wall hanging often depicts a narrative scene, as the Bayeux one shows the Norman Conquest.

clue.text: Jenny? A girl's name

parts.note: Jenny Lind was a famous nineteenth-century Swedish soprano, the 'Swedish Nightingale'

explanation.surface: Someone asks whether Jenny is one particular girl's name.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jenny' looks like the definition but supplies the singer's surname, Lind.
explanation.definitionFit: Linda is a common female first name.

clue.text: Test rock-like substance — no carbon found

indicators.note: no here means the named element is missing from the substance, so its letter is struck out

parts.note: coral is the hard, rock-like skeleton built up by marine polyps
C is the chemical symbol for carbon

explanation.surface: A lab report: a test on a stony sample found it contained no carbon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'no' takes C out of CORAL; 'found' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: An oral is a spoken examination, a kind of test given out loud by an examiner.

clue.text: Time ran out to get some clothing

indicators.note: out suggests the letters are put out of order, scrambled into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: Time ran out before someone could buy new clothes.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old word for garments or clothing.

clue.text: To walk with one friend is permitted

parts.note: to leg it is informal for going on foot, walking or running
I is the Roman numeral for one
a mate is a friend

explanation.surface: A rule says strolling alongside a friend is allowed.
explanation.definitionFit: Legitimate means lawful or allowed, a synonym of permitted.

clue.text: Little Mary I had found to be bombastic

parts.note: 'little Mary' is old British slang for the stomach, from a J. M. Barrie play; TUM is the tummy
I'd is the contraction of I had

explanation.surface: Someone discovers a girl called Mary was pompous and overblown in her speech.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Little Mary' looks like a small girl but is dated British slang for the stomach, from J. M. Barrie's play of that name.
explanation.definitionFit: Tumid literally means swollen, and figuratively describes inflated, pompous language.

clue.text: Criticise one about to meet monarch for being alarmed

parts.note: to pan a play or film is to criticise it harshly
I is the Roman numeral for one
C is short for circa, Latin for about
a king is a monarch

explanation.surface: Someone is told off for losing their nerve before meeting royalty.
explanation.definitionFit: Panicking is being gripped by sudden fear, the same state as being alarmed.

clue.text: Final initiative to encourage customers to take stock

definitions.text: Final initiative to encourage customers to take stock

parts.words: Final initiative to encourage customers to take stock
parts.note: 'take stock' usually means to review a situation, but here customers literally take the shop's goods in a last sell-off

explanation.definitionFit: A shop holds a sell-off at reduced prices to empty its shelves of goods.

clue.text: Art gallery chaps faced with restrictions — little time for restoration

parts.note: reins are controls or restraints, as in keeping a tight rein
the Tate is a group of London art galleries
men are chaps
T is the abbreviation for time

explanation.surface: Staff at an art gallery face new limits and are left with hardly any time for repair work.
explanation.walkthrough: 'faced with' is only a link joining the pieces; the Tate is Britain's best-known gallery group.
explanation.definitionFit: Reinstatement is putting someone or something back in a former place, which is a restoration.

clue.text: What hospitals offer in choices over a period of time

indicators.note: over here means the choices are laid over and around the period

parts.note: options are choices
an era is a period of time

explanation.surface: A statement about what hospitals provide in the way of choices across a stretch of time.
explanation.definitionFit: Hospitals perform surgical procedures for patients, a service they provide.

clue.text: Woman must have external supports for baskets

indicators.note: external says the supports sit outside, wrapping round the woman's name

parts.note: piers are pillars that support a bridge or building
Ann is a woman's name

explanation.surface: A woman needs outside help to hold up her baskets.
explanation.definitionFit: Panniers are a pair of baskets or bags slung either side of a bicycle or a pack animal.

clue.text: Publicist's satisfied with spin for the time being

parts.note: a PRO is a public relations officer, a publicist

indicators.note: spin turns the word for satisfied round so it reads backwards

parts.note: to meet a demand is to satisfy it, so met means satisfied

explanation.surface: A PR person is content with putting a favourable spin on things, at least for now.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with spin' sounds like PR jargon but reverses MET to TEM.
explanation.definitionFit: Pro tem is short for the Latin pro tempore, meaning temporarily.

clue.text: Frightful bounders led into crime

indicators.note: frightful suggests something wild and disordered, so the letters are thrown into a new order

explanation.surface: Dreadful cads have been led into a life of wrongdoing.
explanation.definitionFit: To suborn is to bribe or induce someone into an unlawful act such as perjury.

clue.text: Wreck silver in wild party

indicators.note: in says the metal is placed inside the word for the party

parts.note: a rave is a wild party
Ag is the chemical symbol for silver

explanation.surface: The family silver gets smashed during an out-of-control party.
explanation.definitionFit: To ravage is to devastate or destroy, a synonym of wreck as a verb.

clue.text: They can see six sheep crossing the river

parts.note: VI is six in Roman numerals

indicators.note: crossing has the sheep straddling the river, so the river letter sits inside them

parts.note: ewes are female sheep
R is the abbreviation for river

explanation.surface: Six sheep are fording a river, watched by onlookers.
explanation.definitionFit: Viewers are people watching, those able to see something.

clue.text: One may go round for a barbecue

definitions.text: One may go round for a barbecue

parts.words: One may go round for a barbecue
parts.note: reads like a guest dropping in for a cookout, but describes a device that rotates meat over a fire

explanation.definitionFit: A turnspit is a rotating rod (or once a person or dog turning it) that roasts meat over flames.

clue.text: Buddy vandalised Rome and another Italian city

parts.note: a pal is a buddy, a friend

indicators.note: vandalised means damaged and broken up, so the letters of the word are reordered

explanation.surface: A friend went on a destructive spree in Rome and then a second Italian city.
explanation.walkthrough: 'another' fits because Rome, also an Italian city, appears in the clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Palermo is the capital of Sicily, an Italian city.

clue.text: The way good intentions cannot improve!

definitions.text: The way good intentions cannot improve!

parts.words: The way good intentions cannot improve!
parts.note: plays on the proverb that the route to damnation is paved with good intentions: it is already paved, so they cannot pave (improve) it further

explanation.walkthrough: 'improve' is used in the sense of making up a road surface; the proverb has the work already done.
explanation.definitionFit: The proverb says this route to damnation is paved with good intentions, so it is the road they surface.

clue.text: "The cloth" is what padre is about

indicators.note: about means the letters are moved around into a different order

explanation.surface: A priest's work concerns 'the cloth', meaning the clergy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The cloth' suggests the clergy, apt for a padre, but the definition is a plain piece of fabric.
explanation.definitionFit: A drape is a hanging piece of fabric, such as a curtain.

clue.text: Emblem of country or town

definitions.meaning: the national emblem of Wales is this vegetable
a market town in Staffordshire, England, bears the same name

explanation.definitionFit: A Welsh national symbol, worn on St David's Day, and also a Staffordshire market town.

clue.text: Maiden possibly tense, being in trouble with the bank?

parts.note: in cricket a maiden is an over in which no runs are scored, so a maiden is an example of an over
drawn means strained or tense, as in a drawn face

explanation.surface: A nervous young woman frets about her standing with the bank.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Maiden' suggests a young woman, but in cricket a maiden is a scoreless over of six balls; 'possibly' marks it as an example.
explanation.definitionFit: An overdrawn account has more taken out than was paid in, which puts the holder in debt to the bank.

clue.text: Sort of bird's nest in a lake

parts.note: Erie is one of the Great Lakes of North America

explanation.surface: A bird's nest is found floating in a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is only a link here; A and ERIE simply sit side by side.
explanation.definitionFit: An aerie (eyrie) is the high nest of an eagle or other bird of prey.

clue.text: Band hard on the heels of special regiment

indicators.note: on the heels of means following directly behind, so this letter comes after the regiment

parts.note: the SAS is the Special Air Service, a British special forces regiment
H is the abbreviation for hard, as on pencils

explanation.surface: A tough band of soldiers follows close behind the elite special forces.
explanation.definitionFit: A sash is a band of cloth worn round the waist or over the shoulder.

clue.text: Business in which everything's sewn up?

definitions.text: Business in which everything's sewn up?

parts.words: Business in which everything's sewn up?
parts.note: 'sewn up' usually means a deal settled in advance, but here it is literal: stitching with thread

explanation.definitionFit: Needlework is sewing and embroidery, an occupation where every piece is literally stitched.
